name: ConversionRatio
summary: Reifies the factor between two units as an object, so that converting a quantity is looking something up rather than knowing it.

roles.name: ConversionRatio
roles.summary: The factor from one unit to another, held as data. Figure 3.3 gives it two distinct ends and a number, which is the whole of it — and the reason it is worth having is that conversions written as code are written once per place that needs one, while a ratio held as an object is stated once and composed.

roles.name: From
roles.summary: The unit converted out of. Naming which end is which is the assertion: both ends are units, nothing distinguishes them, and an inverted ratio is a factor applied upside down — which produces a plausible number rather than an error.

roles.name: To
roles.summary: The unit converted into, and never the same as the one converted out of.
